theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks rank #2 and are eligible with the strongest combination of trend-health legs: durability_bar 0.70, breadth 0.714, and a mixed hurst tag. The absolute-trend gate (the only validated risk-control edge here) supports staying with an eligible, broad-based topic rather than the thin leader. This is a relative stability lean, not a return forecast.
theses.dissent: Financials are crowded adjacent (crowding_z 0.42) and rate-sensitive; if macro AI/tech narrative pulls capital to growth, banks could lag on a relative basis regardless of their own trend health.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO underperforms XEG.TO by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Utilities & Renewables
theses.thesis: Utilities & Renewables is eligible, rank 6, with the strongest trend signature in the whole panel: durability_bar 0.81, breadth 0.917, hurst_tag trend, and uncrowded (crowding_z -0.27, crowded false). Momentum rank is a focus lens only, so low score does not disqualify a durable trend structure.
theses.dissent: Defensives like utilities often imply a risk-off rotation bid; if the broader TSX rallies on energy and financial cyclicals, utilities' low momentum score may persist and lag badly.

falsifier.text: XUT.TO makes a 2-week low against the S&P/TSX benchmark before the check-by date

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas is the rank-1 leader but shows a mean-revert hurst tag, zero breadth (0.0), and thin durability_bar (0.41). The leader is not a buy just because it leads — momentum rank is not edge. With the validated absolute-trend gate the only real control, this thin, mean-reverting structure argues for NOT chasing, especially with a one-narrative flag false and absorption only 0.33.
